- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., recent sentiment change > 0.5) and news volume is high, model tends to overestimate prices — apply downward bias correction.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If sentiment is consistently negative or volatile (e.g., sentiment change > 0.5 or < -0.5 over 3+ days), model underestimates — add 0.5–1.5% upward bias.
- Model underperforms when sentiment is flat or news volume is low — adjust forecast upward by 0.3–0.8% to account for hidden market momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags by 1–3 days — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending upward.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day windows — if model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.7) and news volume is low, model tends to underestimate — add 0.5–1.0% to forecast.
